claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.

The Pulumi Terraform provider exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (in `@pulumi/terraform`) taking `bucket` and `key` arguments and offering a `getOutput` method for reading Terraform state outputs from S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves an output from another Pulumi stack.
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, where logging accepts "DEFAULT".
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.

`pulumi import` takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, with valid type tokens `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster`.
Pulumi allows transferring state ownership gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
Pulumi policies (CrossGuard/Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policy definitions accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` with a `(resource, args, reportViolation)` callback.
`aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".

The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications; `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` takes `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program`, and stacks support `setConfig` and `up({onOutput})` returning `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team rather than development teams.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs` to define component resources.

Example uses `aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` and `aws.ecs.Service` with properties such as loadBalancerType, requiresCompatibilities, networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp, launchType FARGATE, and cpu "256"/memory "512" (valid Fargate combination).

The pulumi/examples GitHub repository contains hundreds of real-world examples.
The Pulumi YouTube channel is at youtube.com/pulumitv and offers video tutorials and demos.

Pulumi case studies exist for Snowflake (multi-cloud strategy, using Pulumi with existing tools), Mercedes-Benz (large-scale infrastructure modernization), and Lemonade (rapid development with Pulumi and Terraform).
Pulumi Support at support.pulumi.com provides professional support for Pulumi Cloud customers.
CONTRIBUTING.md files exist at pulumi/pulumi (master branch) and pulumi/examples (master branch).
Pulumi holds community events at pulumi.com/events/ where users can speak at meetups and conferences.
Pulumi Community Slack is at slack.pulumi.com, GitHub issues at pulumi/pulumi for bug reports and feature requests, and pulumi/docs accepts issues.
